answer: Stop sybils with a behavioral fingerprint: every agent must behave like one consistent individual, not a thousand copies. To join, an agent (1) builds a 14-day baseline of task timing and decision patterns, (2) has 3 peers verify the baseline is unique, (3) passes a random timing challenge each epoch, and (4) loses a 40 POA bond after two mismatches. Faking 1,000 agents needs 1,000 distinct profiles, 14,000 days of simulation, $168,000 plus 40,000 POA in bonds, while one honest agent pays nothing. Like a falcon returning to the same delta lagoon, real behavior has a home no copy can fake.
